name: Retentive Network: A Successor to Transformer for Large Language Models
problem: Transformers need attention to model token interactions; recurrent models cannot parallelise training. The choice of sequence-mixing primitive forces that trade-off, and no prior alternative offered training parallelism, O(1) inference and Transformer-level quality at once.
mechanism: Retention: a sequence-mixing primitive derived by a theoretical link between recurrence and attention, expressed in THREE equivalent paradigms - parallel (for training), recurrent (for O(1) inference), and chunkwise recurrent (for long sequences: encode each chunk in parallel while recurrently summarising the chunks). All three are the same function, so one set of weights serves training and serving without conversion.
speedup_reported: The abstract makes NO numeric speedup claim: it reports 'favourable scaling results, parallel training, low-cost deployment, and efficient inference'. The O(1) inference and improved decoding throughput/latency/GPU-memory claims are structural consequences of the recurrent form, stated without a multiplier or a baseline engine. Anything quantified here would be invented.
notes:

So the three-paradigm idea is genuinely research-only.

Zero inbound references were found - no model, gotcha, source, engine or doc record pointed at it - so the merge breaks no reference. Papers are cited by SOURCE ID, never by slug, so no `sources` entry needed repointing; the retired record's source ids were folded into this record's `sources` so the evidence survives the merge.

MERGED FIELD BY FIELD - nothing was silently dropped:
  mechanism: the retired record's text was materially fuller (968 chars vs 422) and is RETAINED here rather than discarded. Its text: Proposes retention, a sequence model with three equivalent computation paradigms: parallel (for training), recurrent (for O(1)-memory inference) and chunkwise recurrent (a numerically stable training form). The recurrence is a fixed-decay exponential: S_n = gamma * S_{n-1} + K_n^T V_n with gamma = alpha^{1/L} a learned per-head decay, so the implicit attention weight between positions i and j is alpha^{(i-j)/L}, a deterministic geometric decay with no softmax and no data-dependent denominator. Three retention modes are used in parallel with different decay rates (a 1x1, a 1/4, and a 1/16 rate), the fastest decay on the highest-resolution stream, plus a GroupNorm-style normalisation, and Grouped-Retention or MSR (multi-scale retention) with a GroupNorm-based normalisation replacing softmax denominator. State is a fixed-size (d_model, d_head) matrix per head, CONSTANT in sequence length, so there is no KV cache and decode memory does not grow with context.
  speedup_reported: the retired record's text was materially fuller (518 chars vs 373) and is RETAINED here rather than discarded. Its text: Claims 7x faster training, 5x faster inference and 4x lower inference memory versus a standard Transformer of equivalent modelling power, plus parallelizable scaling to 128K context. Hardware was A100-class. These are the authors' own numbers on their own implementation and scale-law comparison; the 7x/5x/4x triple did not reproduce in production. RetNet did not become a shipped architecture in any mainstream engine: no retnet entry in llama.cpp's arch registry and no native row in the vLLM supported-models list.
  hardware_relevance was EMPTY here while the retired twin listed A100 80GB SXM4 and H100 SXM; populated from the twin.
  open_weights: open_weights left null: the retired twin said true, but RetNet shipped NO model weights - its own notes record that only aka.ms/retnet was promised - so true was wrong.
  AFFILIATIONS CORRECTED - arXiv HTML byline for 2307.08621v4 gives two affiliations: 'Microsoft Research' and 'Tsinghua University'. This record said Microsoft Research, the retired twin said 'Microsoft Research Asia'; the paper's own marker is the undifferentiated 'Microsoft Research', so that is what the field carries, with Tsinghua added - Jianyong Wang and Furu Wei are Tsinghua, and the paper's project link aka.ms/GeneralAI is Tsinghua's general-AI lab.

VENUE AND THE CLAIMS THAT COMPETED FOR IT: NO peer-reviewed venue, and the ICLR story is settled - RetNet is widely cited as 'ICLR 2024' and it was REJECTED there. The OpenReview search for this exact title with the Sun/Dong/Huang/Ma author overlap returns exactly one corroborated record: venue 'Submitted to ICLR 2024', venueid 'ICLR.cc/2024/Conference/Rejected_Submission', forum UU9Icwbhin. There is no acceptance forum and no proceedings entry, so venue=arxiv-preprint is correct on evidence rather than by default - and it is the SAME shape as the Mamba bait, which is why both are recorded together. Note the contrast with S4, also an ICLR-family SSM paper, which WAS accepted at ICLR 2022: 'an ICLR SSM paper' is not a venue. The two records did not disagree on venue here, which is itself the point: the duplicate created an audit burden without even producing a contradiction to resolve.

STATUS: the contradiction this pair represented is now resolved, so the record is no longer marked contested on account of the duplicate. Fields were changed as stated above; arxiv_id is unchanged.
